thread:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — we need to finalize the affinity cutover playbook for multi-tenant isolation. Sales wants firm migration windows to promise customers. Draft below, open to scope cuts.
Jin (Eng-Runtime): Agree. I sketched a minimal cutover: enable per-tenant affinity, small canary, expand. Shortlist: canary %s, SLA impact, fallback, observability hooks.
Raj (SRE): We need rollback gates and a soft-eviction path if a slice overloads. Also plan for cross-region failover during cutover.
Alex (Sales): Key ask from enterprise pilots: guaranteed 2-hour window for cutover and a hotline with eng during the first 48h. Can we commit? Customers will pay for scheduling.
Marta (Security): Also need to validate that tenancy isolation preserves audit logs and KMS boundaries during migration. If private deployments involved, we require an on-prem checklist.
Jin (Eng-Runtime): Proposed minimal playbook (rough):
```
affinity_cutover_v1:
  prechecks:
    - capacity-reservation: true
    - kv-cache-warm: true
  steps:
    - canary: 3% tenants for 30m
    - monitor: latency, error-rate, token-cost
    - expand: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (30m hold at each)
  rollback_if:
    - p50_latency_increase > 50ms
    - error_rate > 2% for 5m
  fallback_route: shared-model-pool
  observability: tracing, per-tenant cost-breakdown
```
Raj (SRE): Need to add circuit-breaker for KV-cache pressure and a hard cap on simultaneous migrations. Also define who hits the rollback button (SRE+Runtime lead).
Maya (PM): Can we make the canary configurable per customer? Some customers want more aggressive (10%) if they pay for dedicated capacity.
Jin (Eng-Runtime): Yes — config flag: `cutover.canary_pct` and `cutover.escalation_contact`. Implementation risk: we'll need per-tenant routing policy eval in the router (cheap but touches hot path).
Marta (Security): For private deployments, include: KMS transfer validation, no outbound telemetry to Redwood control plane during cutover unless allowed.
Alex (Sales): Good. Sales handshake: we can offer a "managed cutover" add-on — 2-hour window + eng standby for a premium. Need SLAs and pricing sketch.
Maya (PM): Launch criteria checklist proposal (short):
- Signed scoping doc with customer (includes window & fallback)
- Capacity reservation validated by SRE
- Rollback & playbook runbook published
- Observability dashboards + alert thresholds agreed
- Security checklist passed (KMS/audit)
- Sales acceptance & billing terms
If any of these fail, cutover is postponed. Thoughts?
Raj (SRE): Add "load test run against isolated slice" to prechecks. Also need an emergency evacuation playbook to move tenants back to shared pool without cache loss.
Jin (Eng-Runtime): One more technical note: routing policy example for rollout: 
```
- match: tenant_id in customer_list
  action: route_to: slice-v2
  fallback: route_to: shared
  max_wait_ms: 150
```
This requires router to evaluate tenant ACLs atomically during update. We'll need traffic-manager rollout to be atomic per region.
Alex (Sales): Can we make the managed cutover include a rehearsed dry-run with the customer (no traffic) so we can bill for that too? Most enterprise customers want a rehearsal.
Maya (PM): Yes, add rehearsal to playbook (pre-checks).
Marta (Security): Confirming: rehearsal must still run kms/audit validations.
ops-bot: deployment-notice: "traffic-manager v2 flagged for staged rollout (flags: slice-affinity). Scheduled: 2026-06-02T10:00:00Z"
Jin (Eng-Runtime): Timeline ask: we can land the router evaluation and the cutover flags in two sprints if we prioritize. But per-tenant atomic update needs a tiny coordination service — estimate 3w dev + 1w canary.
Maya (PM): OK — PM asks for prioritized backlog: 1) router atomic eval 2) canary config + obs hooks 3) rollback automation 4) docs + sales page.
Alex (Sales): I'll draft the managed cutover pricing and handshake template. Will share by EOD tomorrow.
Raj (SRE): I'll draft emergency evacuation steps and add load test to prechecks.
Marta (Security): I'll prepare security signoff checklist and KMS validation steps.
Jin (Eng-Runtime): I'll open RFC for the router change and include sample configs and perf estimates.
Maya (PM): Perfect. Last item: negotiation point with product leadership — do we gate advanced per-tenant affinity to Dedicated/Private customers only for first 6 months? This reduces blast radius and simplifies support. Opinions?
Alex (Sales): Sales vote: gate to Dedicated/Private initially. Easier to monetize and manage expectations.
Raj (SRE): Technical vote: gate it at first, unless we see a lot of low-risk customers. Good to limit blast radius.
Marta (Security): Gate it. Private customers have stricter KMS/audit needs anyway.
Maya (PM): Sounds like consensus. I'll mark the initiative as "early access for Dedicated/Private" and proceed with the playbook above. I'll follow up with a short RFC link once Jin posts it. Thanks all :thumbsup:
